name: High-Bar Barbell Back Squat
setup: Bar high on the upper traps (not low on the rear delts). Unrack, take a moderate stance with toes turned out as needed for comfort, set the feet, breathe in and tighten the abdominals so the torso stays upright and the spine neutral.
execution: Break at the hips and knees together, sit back a little and plenty down, and let the knees travel forward over the toes. Control the descent to a standardized depth (at least just below parallel, or as deep as you can keep a neutral spine and flat feet). Stand up, breathing out in the last half of the ascent or at the top.
cues: Hit the same depth landmark every rep
Chest does not cave forward; back neutral or slightly arched
Stay on the whole foot, heels and toes down
Break hips and knees at the same time; knees may pass the toes
Breathe in at the top, tighten, breathe out in the last half of the ascent
Pause at the bottom and settle onto the heels if you drift to your toes
errors: Cutting depth at an arbitrary point
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Going deeper than your hips and ankles allow, so the pelvis tucks or you go on your toes
Not bracing, or over-bracing on every rep of a 5-15 rep set
Different depth or cadence every rep
Looking straight down or straight up behind you, which costs balance
Excess forward lean from sitting back too far
why: Coach frames it as a quad-hypertrophy squat; high bar keeps the torso upright and the quads the limiting factor.

name: Walking Dumbbell Lunge
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Stand tall. Plan a step of roughly one yard (a metre) to start, then adjust.
execution: Step forward into a long but stable step. Lower with a controlled descent of about two seconds until the back knee gently touches the floor, keeping the torso upright and still. Stand up, stop the trailing leg beside the lead leg instead of swinging it through, then step into the next rep.
cues: Back knee gently touches the floor every rep
Step about a yard (a metre), long enough to feel a stretch but still stable
Keep the upper body upright and level, including on the way up
Stop the trailing leg and reset each rep rather than swinging it through
errors: Inconsistent range of motion from rep to rep
Step too short (squat-like, more knee shear)
Step so long you lose stability
Falling into the bottom of each rep
Tilting the torso forward to recruit the back and hamstrings
Banging the knee onto the floor
Grip, traps or collapse forward ending the set before the legs do
why: Coach targets glutes, adductors and quads, in roughly that order.
